messages:
Sam (PM): BetaCo saw interactive chat jitter during their demo. They want a minimal launch plan: p95 <= 150ms for interactive sessions. Can we scope a short path this sprint?
Maya (Eng): Quick numbers from prod slice: p50=70ms p95=380ms p99=820ms. Heavy tail when sessions exceed ~120 tokens. Cause: repeated KV fetches + attention on long prefixes.
Ollie (SRE): Note: reducing batch wait helps p95 but can crush throughput. We need canary + circuit-breaker to avoid noisy neighbor effects.
Priya (Product): Let's run RICE on three options: cache-first, quant+kernel, reserved low-latency lane. Cache seems highest speed-to-value.
Diego (ML): Micro-quant (q8/q4 hybrid) + kernel tuning can drop single-token latency ~20-30% but needs eval on BetaCo prompts for quality. Confidence medium.
Maya (Eng): Proposal: implement prefix cache + adaptive batching + a demo-time session throttle. Canary plan: 48h, 5% traffic, monitor p50/p95/p99 and quality samples.
Maya (Eng): Canary sketch:
```
route: beta-lowlatency-canary
traffic: 5%
features: [prefix_cache, session_ttl=300s, batch_max_ms=6, throttle_long_sessions=true]
metrics: p50/p95/p99, user-drop-rate, sampled QA checks
duration: 48h
rollback: p95>180ms OR QA regressions
```
Ollie (SRE): Add global circuit-breaker: if cluster p95 increases >8% during canary, auto-disable and drain canary hosts. Also tag metrics for quick ops runbook.
Priya (Product): Quick RICE calc: cache-first highest score, quant has broad reach but lower confidence, dedicated lane is fallback for SLA-paying customers.
Sam (PM): Actions: 1) Maya -> open PR + small smoke tests (due Thu). 2) Diego -> run 48h quant eval on BetaCo prompts. 3) O llie -> canary runbook + circuit-breaker. 4) Priya -> check BetaCo willingness to pay for reserved lane if needed. Reconvene Mon.
